name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Cooldown Landmines: Cross-Tenant Interference Attacks on LLM Gateways
items.dek: LiteLLM gateways sharing cooldown records allow cross-tenant attacks forcing fallback or denial; tenant-scoped cooldown with origin checks mitigates the gap.
items.unproven: attacks demonstrated on LiteLLM; effectiveness against other LLM gateway implementations and with hardened authentication policies not tested

items.title: Correct Verdicts, Flawed Reasoning: Structured Auditing of LLM-based Vulnerability Reasoning
items.dek: 60% of correct LLM vulnerability verdicts rest on fabricated reasoning; structured output auditing catches failures that free-form CoT conceals.
items.unproven: VERA's performance on proprietary or novel vulnerability classes; integration into live SAST/DAST pipelines; cost of structured output overhead at scale.

items.title: Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders
items.dek: Maliciously modified sparse autoencoders can inject code backdoors into language models without changing the model itself.
items.unproven: Supply-chain detection mechanisms and defense deployment feasibility in real SDLC pipelines not addressed.

items.title: Runaway Reaction: When Benign Skills Compose into Malicious Behavior
items.dek: Composing benign agent skills can create malicious behaviors not present in any individual skill, even after vetting.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to skill repositories tested; generalization to closed or proprietary skill ecosystems not demonstrated.

items.title: Blocking at the Boundary: Auditing Long-Horizon Agents against Staged Prompt Injection
items.dek: Claude Code and Codex are vulnerable to staged prompt injection across long workflows; blocking requires boundary action auditing before each consequential action, not pre- or post-execution screening.
items.unproven: evaluated on two model families in native runtimes; effectiveness against fine-tuned or system-prompted variants not established

items.title: VulValidate: Auditing Function-Level Vulnerability Labels with Executable Evidence
items.dek: Auditing 35,849 labeled vulnerable functions in BigVul, PrimeVul, and DiverseVul confirms 57.2%, corrects 19.0%, and reclassifies 22.3%; expert review supports 90–99% of decisions.
items.unproven: corrected dataset contains 15,890 distinct functions; representativeness of expert panel and generalization to future vulnerability datasets not established

items.title: WLPA: A Network Management Framework for Allocating Scarce Quantum-Safe Link Postures under Weakest-Link Exposure
items.dek: Algorithm for allocating scarce QKD and quantum-safe link upgrades under weakest-link exposure; identifies when per-link heuristics fail.
items.unproven: application to networks larger than 20,000 links; integration with real-world migration planning tools and compliance frameworks

items.title: CVE-2026-88779 — Citrix NetScaler Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer Vulnerability
items.dek: Citrix NetScaler. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 7 October.

items.title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? Evidence from Nonpublic Vulnerabilities and Subsequent Attacks
items.dek: AI models tested on nonpublic vulnerabilities show variable exploit-versus-repair performance, with 92 of 524 follow-up attacks succeeding after initial patch.
items.unproven: Whether results generalize across vulnerability classes and whether lab exploit generation tracks real attacker capability in active campaigns.

items.title: RAISED: Self-Distillation for Robustness to Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
items.dek: RAISED self-distillation mitigates prompt injection in tool-using agents by matching clean behavior without distribution drift on benign tasks.
items.unproven: Robustness against adaptive attacks or to agents in active production SDLCs; evaluation on agent types beyond the tested scenarios.

items.title: Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? Localizing the Origins of Silent Failures in Agentic Vulnerability Repair
items.dek: Trace-based method locates where LLM repair agents first diverge from security intent in silent failures; most trace to unaddressed requirements, not code writes.
items.unproven: ground truth for 5 of 95 failures and potential labeler bias; generalization beyond SecurityEval and CVEfixes; applicability when agent frameworks lack execution traces.

items.title: Visual Grounding Safety in Vision-Language Models
items.dek: Vision-language models refuse harmful requests 31–59 percentage points more often in text form than when asked to output bounding boxes or points.
items.unproven: whether this gap persists across production deployment patterns and whether fine-tuning generalizes beyond the three benchmarks tested.

items.title: The Poisoned Conversation: Privacy-Leaking Watermarks in Unified Multimodal Models
items.dek: Malicious multimodal models can embed hidden watermarks in later-generated images keyed to earlier sensitive text in the same conversation, leaking privacy from local deployments.
items.unproven: whether detection remains feasible under adversarial watermark design and whether practical deployment scenarios encounter this threat model.

items.title: Who Is Your Agent Serving? Provider-Side Indirect Prompt Injection in Proactive Agents
items.dek: External providers can redirect proactive agents toward their targets by controlling only their own content, gaining up to 77.4 percentage-point increases in target authorization.
items.unproven: tested only on simulated user models in three controlled environments; unclear how real users would respond to such attacks in production deployment

items.title: Invisible Ink, Visible Lies: How Production Watermarking Causes LLMs to Hallucinate
items.dek: Six text-watermarking methods induce hallucination via token perturbations and attention drift; two plug-in mitigations proposed but not evaluated.
items.unproven: effectiveness of proposed interventions; interaction with watermarking deployments already in production systems

items.title: TranScope: What the Software Hides About LLM Training Data, the Hardware Reveals at Scale, and Accelerators Magnify
items.dek: Hardware side-channels reveal training-data membership in constant-time LLMs via microarchitecture footprints at scale.
items.unproven: Whether the signal survives real-world deployment noise, defenses, or practical threat models where an attacker has black-box hardware access but no privilege.

items.title: Efficient HQC Implementations on RISC-V: A Cross-Layer Design Space Exploration
items.dek: RISC-V HQC implementations achieve 4.8x to 69.6x improvements across 29,920 architectural configurations on FPGA.
items.unproven: Results limited to FPGA synthesis; production silicon performance and power consumption under operational constraints not established.

items.title: Compromise Is Not Consequence: Evaluating Task-Scoped Authorization in LLM Agents with Paired Replay
items.dek: Task-scoped authorization (JWT, sender-constrained tokens) blocks harmful LLM agent tool execution while broad bearer tokens fail (8.9–37.8%).
items.unproven: 128 lab scenarios with five local models; scalability to production scale, multi-tenant deployments, and sophisticated prompt injection not established.

items.title: AgentDoxx: Agentic Re-identification of Anonymized Text with Web Search
items.dek: Agentic LLMs re-identify 88% of anonymized transcripts once a target appears in web search results, with entity masking failing on 85% of samples.
items.unproven: whether synthetic transcripts reflect real anonymization patterns and whether defenses beyond entity masking reduce the attack surface.

items.title: Don't Judge an LLM Only by Its Activations: Discovering Suppressed Safety Features via Counterfactual Activation Potential
items.dek: Inactive neural features suppress safety refusals in LLMs; flipping suppressed features turns compliance attacks invisible to standard mechanistic interpretability tools.
items.unproven: whether this attack succeeds against defenses deployed in production systems and generalizes across model families beyond those tested.

items.title: Red-TTT: Test-Time Training for Automated Jailbreaking Large Language Models
items.dek: Test-time training adapts an attacker's parameters mid-jailbreak by gradient steps on each round, consolidating discoveries about victim behavior instead of discarding them.
items.unproven: whether adaptive attacks remain practical under deployment constraints and whether defenses designed for fixed attackers generalize to online-adapted ones.

items.title: What a Policy Gate Can and Cannot Know: Measured Boundaries of Cross-Platform Command Adjudication
items.dek: Policy gates adjudicating agent actions without parsing syntax remain vulnerable to carrier and mapping differences; a Linux audit found 43 re-expressions and four unmapped escapes.
items.unproven: limited to one gateway design and Linux twin environment; generalizability to other policy frameworks and operating systems unclear

items.title: Characterizing Security Effects of OSS Vulnerabilities in Agent Systems
items.dek: OSS vulnerabilities in agent tool dependencies propagate security effects through tool outputs, agent state, and model exposure; runtime provenance can trace effect boundaries.
items.unproven: taxonomy derived from qualitative investigation; no quantification of how often effects propagate to consequential model outputs or how frequently agents exercise vulnerable paths

items.title: Hidden Risks of Jev: An Empirical Study of Security, Privacy, and Dual Use
items.dek: Prompt injection, training-data poisoning, and information leakage attacks on LLM decision layers; defenses untested in production.
items.unproven: whether attacks scale beyond the controlled test setup or whether proposed mitigations work at deployment scale

items.title: Runtime Authorization of Self-Generated Subgoals in Long-Horizon Tool-Using AI Agents
items.dek: Authorization mechanism for AI agents that replan dynamically; prevents goal-graph drift outside approved scope via witness-based contracts.
items.unproven: applicability beyond the finite structured domain tested; scalability to real-world agent deployments with free-form objectives
